This chicken burrito bowl is one of those meals that genuinely does everything right. You get 40 grams of protein per serving, it costs around $2.80 to make, and it comes together in under 30 minutes. Meal prep gold.
Why This Recipe Works # Chicken thighs are cheaper than chicken breasts and stay juicy even after reheating, which makes them perfect for batch cooking. Canned black beans and rice bulk up the bowl without adding much cost at all. The seasoning does the heavy lifting here, so every bite tastes like something you paid twice as much for.
Ingredients # 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs 1 cup white rice (dry) 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed 1 cup frozen corn 1/2 cup salsa (jarred) 1 tsp chili powder 1 tsp cumin 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/2 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp salt 1 tbsp olive oil 1/4 cup shredded Mexican cheese blend Estimated cost per serving: $2.80 (makes 3 servings)
Instructions # Cook the rice according to package directions. While it cooks, move on to the chicken. Pat your chicken thighs dry with a paper towel. Mix together the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and salt in a small bowl, then rub the spice mix all over the chicken. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred on the outside. Internal temp should hit 165°F. Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then slice or chop it into bite-sized pieces. In the same skillet, add the drained black beans and frozen corn. Cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is warmed through. Build your bowls: start with a scoop of rice, then add the bean and corn mixture, followed by the chicken. Top with salsa and shredded cheese. Serve immediately or portion into meal prep containers. Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 520 Protein 40g Carbs 52g Fat 14g Cost Per Serving $2.80 Tips # Buy chicken thighs in bulk when they go on sale. You can freeze them flat in a zip-lock bag and pull out exactly what you need. This is one of the easiest ways to cut your per-serving cost even further. Meal prep this for the whole week. Store the components separately if you can, but if you mix them together, they keep well in the fridge for up to 4 days. The flavors actually get better by day two. Swap white rice for brown rice if you want more fiber. It takes longer to cook but adds a little extra nutrition without changing the cost much. Add a squeeze of lime and some cilantro if you have them on hand. Neither is required, but both make the bowl taste noticeably fresher. Make a batch of these bowls on Sunday and you will thank yourself every single day of the week.

If you want a week of high-protein lunches without spending a fortune, these ground turkey meal prep bowls are your answer. Each bowl clocks in at around 40 grams of protein and costs under $3 to make. Prep them Sunday and you’re set for the whole week.
Why This Recipe Works # Ground turkey is one of the best budget protein sources you can buy, especially when you catch it on sale. Paired with rice and black beans, you get a complete amino acid profile plus plenty of fiber to keep you full. The seasoning is simple but bold, so these bowls actually taste good on day four.
Ingredients # Makes 5 servings
2 lbs 93% lean ground turkey 2 cups dry white rice 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed 1 cup frozen corn 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained 1 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp chili powder 1/2 tsp smoked paprika Salt and pepper to taste Optional toppings: salsa, hot sauce, plain Greek yogurt (in place of sour cream) Estimated cost per serving: $2.60
Instructions # Cook the rice. Combine 2 cups dry rice with 4 cups water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 18 minutes. Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Brown the turkey. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey and break it apart with a spatula. Cook for 7 to 9 minutes until no pink remains.
Season the meat. Drain any excess liquid from the skillet. Add garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir everything together and cook for another 2 minutes so the spices bloom.
Add the remaining ingredients. Stir in the drained black beans, frozen corn, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the corn is heated through and everything is well combined.
Portion into containers. Divide the rice evenly among 5 meal prep containers (roughly 3/4 cup cooked rice each). Top each with an even portion of the turkey mixture.
Store and reheat. Seal containers and refrigerate for up to 5 days. Reheat in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway through. Add your toppings after reheating.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 520 Protein 40g Carbs 55g Fat 11g Cost Per Serving $2.60 Nutrition is estimated and will vary based on specific brands and optional toppings.
Tips # Buy turkey in bulk when it goes on sale. Most grocery stores run ground turkey deals weekly. Buy two or three pounds, cook what you need, and freeze the rest raw for next week. Swap the rice for cauliflower rice if you want to cut carbs. It will lower the calorie count by about 150 calories per bowl and is easy to find frozen for under $2 a bag. Double the spice blend and store it in a jar. Having your own premixed taco-style seasoning saves time on future meal preps and cuts down on the number of containers you dig through. Add a squeeze of lime before eating. It sounds minor but a little acid brightens the whole bowl, especially on day three or four when the flavors have had time to meld together. Make these once and you’ll have them in your regular rotation for good.

Shakshuka is one of those meals that looks way more impressive than the effort it takes. This version clocks in at 32g of protein per serving and costs around $2.30 a plate, thanks to eggs, canned chickpeas, and a little feta doing the heavy lifting. It’s ready in 30 minutes and works just as well for dinner as it does for a weekend brunch.
Why This Recipe Works # Eggs are one of the cheapest protein sources you can buy, and pairing them with chickpeas doubles the protein without adding much cost. The spiced tomato base is deeply flavorful from pantry staples you already have on hand. This is a one-pan meal, which means less cleanup and more time enjoying your food.
Ingredients # 6 large eggs 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes 1 small yellow onion, diced 4 cloves garlic, minced 2 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp chili flakes (optional) Salt and pepper to taste 2 oz crumbled feta cheese Fresh parsley for topping (optional) Makes 3 servings. Estimated cost per serving: ~$2.30
Instructions # Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until softened. Add the minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili flakes. Stir for about 60 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir everything together. Season with salt and pepper. Add the drained chickpeas and stir to combine. Let the sauce simmer for 8 to 10 minutes so it thickens up. Use a spoon to make 6 small wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well. Cover the pan and cook on medium-low for 7 to 10 minutes. Pull it off the heat when the whites are set but the yolks are still a little runny. Cook longer if you want firm yolks. Top with crumbled feta and fresh parsley. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread or pita. Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 420 Protein 32g Carbs 34g Fat 18g Cost Per Serving ~$2.30 Tips # Bulk it up with cottage cheese. Stir 1/2 cup of full-fat cottage cheese into the tomato sauce before adding the eggs. It melts right in, adds creaminess, and bumps the protein even higher. Don’t skip the simmer. Letting the sauce cook down before you add the eggs makes a huge difference in flavor. Give it those full 10 minutes. Meal prep friendly. Make the tomato and chickpea base ahead of time and refrigerate it for up to 4 days. Just reheat, crack in fresh eggs, and you have dinner in 15 minutes. Go easy on the heat. Cooking the eggs on medium-low with the lid on gives you the most control. High heat will cook the yolks too fast before the whites are fully set. Make this once and it will earn a permanent spot in your weeknight rotation.

This lentil soup is one of the hardest-working recipes on this blog. Each serving clocks in at 27 grams of protein and costs you roughly $1.75, and one big batch covers your lunches for the entire week. If you’re trying to hit your protein goals without blowing your grocery budget, this one belongs in your regular rotation.
Why This Recipe Works # Lentils are an absolute steal at around $1.50 per pound, and they’re loaded with plant-based protein and fiber that keeps you full for hours. Pairing them with canned chickpeas bumps the protein even higher without adding much cost. The whole pot comes together in about 40 minutes with zero fancy equipment required.
Ingredients # 1 1/2 cups dry green or brown lentils 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes 4 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth 2 cups water 1 medium yellow onion, diced 3 cloves garlic, minced 2 medium carrots, sliced 2 tsp olive oil 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp smoked paprika Salt and pepper to taste Estimated cost per serving: $1.75 (based on 6 servings per batch)
Instructions # Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and carrots. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion softens.
Add the minced garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika. Stir everything together and cook for another 60 seconds until fragrant.
Rinse your lentils under cold water and pick out any debris. Add them to the pot along with the diced tomatoes, broth, and water.
Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Let it simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the drained chickpeas and stir them in. Continue simmering for another 5 to 10 minutes until the lentils are completely tender and the soup has thickened up nicely.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. If the soup is thicker than you’d like, add a splash of water or broth and stir.
Let it cool before dividing into meal prep containers. Store in the fridge for up to 5 days or freeze portions for up to 3 months.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 340 Protein 27g Carbs 48g Fat 5g Cost Per Serving $1.75 Tips # Boost protein even more by stirring in 1/2 cup of plain Greek yogurt per bowl right before eating. It adds a creamy texture and about 8 extra grams of protein. Buy lentils in bulk if your grocery store has a bulk bin section. You can often get them for $0.99 per pound or less, which cuts your cost per serving down further. Don’t skip the simmer time. Lentils that aren’t fully cooked will be gritty and hard to digest. When in doubt, give them a few extra minutes. Freeze in single-serve portions using quart-sized zip-lock bags laid flat. They stack neatly and thaw quickly overnight in the fridge. Eating high protein on a budget sounds hard until you see what a can of chickpeas, a pound of ground turkey, or a bag of lentils can actually do for you. This post breaks down one of our favorite go-to meals that delivers 35g of protein, stays under 450 calories, and costs about $2.10 per serving. Let’s get into it.
Why This Recipe Works # Ground turkey and black beans are one of the best budget protein combos you can build a meal around. Turkey is lean, affordable, and absorbs whatever seasoning you throw at it, and black beans add fiber and extra protein without adding much fat or cost. This is the kind of meal you can make on a Sunday and eat four times during the week without getting bored.
Ingredients # This recipe makes 4 servings.
1 lb 93% lean ground turkey (about $4.50/lb) 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed ($0.89) 1 cup long grain white rice, dry ($0.40 for this amount) 1 cup salsa (jarred is fine, $0.60 for this amount) 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp chili powder 1/2 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp salt 1 tbsp olive oil 1/2 cup shredded reduced-fat cheddar cheese ($0.50 for this amount) 2 cups chicken broth, low sodium ($0.30 for this amount) Estimated cost per serving: $2.10
Instructions # Cook the rice according to package directions, but substitute chicken broth for half the water. This adds flavor without extra cost or calories.
While the rice cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey and break it up with a spatula.
Cook the turkey for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fully browned and no pink remains.
Drain any excess liquid from the pan, then add the cumin, garlic powder, chili powder, smoked paprika, and salt. Stir to coat the meat evenly.
Add the black beans and salsa directly to the skillet. Stir everything together and reduce heat to medium-low. Let it simmer for 5 minutes so the flavors come together.
Divide the cooked rice into four meal prep containers or bowls. Top each one with an equal portion of the turkey and bean mixture.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp of shredded cheddar over each bowl and serve warm, or seal the containers and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 445 Protein 35g Carbohydrates 42g Fat 11g Cost Per Serving $2.10 Tips # Swap the rice for cauliflower rice if you want to cut about 80 calories per serving and add a serving of vegetables. It works really well with the bold seasoning in this recipe. Buy ground turkey in bulk when it goes on sale and freeze it in 1 lb portions. This can drop your cost per serving below $1.75 easily. Use pinto beans instead of black beans if that is what you have on hand. The protein and fiber content are nearly identical, and the price is usually the same. Add a handful of frozen corn in step 5 for extra volume and a little sweetness. It costs almost nothing and stretches each serving without affecting the macros much. If you love banh mi but hate spending $12 at a sandwich shop, this bowl is your new best friend. It packs 38 grams of protein per serving and costs less than $3 to make at home. Bright, fresh, and filling, this one earns a permanent spot in your meal prep rotation.
Why This Recipe Works # Ground chicken is one of the cheapest high-protein options at the grocery store, and it soaks up a simple soy-ginger marinade beautifully. Serving it over rice instead of a baguette keeps costs down without sacrificing any of the flavor you love about classic banh mi. The quick-pickled carrots and cucumbers do a lot of heavy lifting here, giving you that punchy, tangy bite with almost zero effort.
Ingredients # 1 lb ground chicken (~$3.50) 2 cups cooked jasmine rice (~$0.30) 2 tbsp soy sauce (~$0.10) 1 tbsp fish sauce (~$0.10) 1 tbsp sriracha (~$0.05) 1 tsp sesame oil (~$0.10) 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated (~$0.10) 2 garlic cloves, minced (~$0.10) 1 cup shredded carrots (~$0.30) 1 cup cucumber, thinly sliced (~$0.40) 3 tbsp rice vinegar (~$0.10) 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (~$0.10) Estimated cost per serving: $2.60 (makes 2 servings)
Instructions # Quick-pickle your veggies. Combine the shredded carrots and sliced cucumber in a bowl with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Stir and set aside for at least 10 minutes while you cook everything else.
Mix your sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, fish sauce, sriracha, sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Set it aside.
Cook the chicken. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and add a light spray of cooking oil. Add the ground chicken and break it up as it cooks. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes until fully cooked through and slightly browned.
Add the sauce. Pour the soy-ginger sauce over the cooked chicken and stir to coat. Let it cook for another 2 minutes so the sauce reduces slightly and coats every bite.
Build your bowls. Divide the cooked rice between two bowls. Top each with half the chicken, then pile on the pickled carrots and cucumbers.
Finish and serve. Scatter fresh cilantro over the top. Add extra sriracha if you want more heat. Serve immediately or pack it up for meal prep.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 520 Protein 38g Carbs 45g Fat 14g Cost Per Serving $2.60 Tips # Meal prep friendly. Store the pickled veggies separately from the rice and chicken so nothing gets soggy. Everything keeps well in the fridge for up to 4 days. Swap the protein. Ground turkey or canned chicken breast work great here if ground chicken is not in stock or is priced higher at your store. Double the pickle. The quick-pickled carrots and cucumbers are genuinely addictive. Make a double batch and keep them in the fridge all week to throw on anything. Watch your rice. Day-old rice that has been chilled actually holds up better in bowls and meal prep containers. It keeps the texture from getting mushy when everything is packed together. If you want juicy, fall-apart chicken ready to eat all week without spending more than $2.50 a serving, this is your recipe. Each serving packs 38 grams of protein and takes about 10 minutes of actual hands-on work. Let the slow cooker do the rest.
Why This Recipe Works # Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are one of the cheapest cuts at the grocery store, and they shine in a slow cooker because the fat keeps them moist over a long cook. You get big flavor with minimal effort, and the leftovers reheat beautifully for lunches and dinners all week. No dry chicken, no complicated prep.
Ingredients # 3 lbs bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 6 thighs) 1 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp onion powder 1 tsp smoked paprika 1 tsp dried Italian seasoning 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp black pepper 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth 4 cloves garlic, minced 1 medium onion, sliced Estimated cost per serving: $2.40 (based on 6 servings, pricing from major US grocery chains as of mid-2026)
Instructions # Season the chicken. Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Rub them all over with olive oil, then coat evenly with garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Optional sear for extra flavor. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the thighs skin-side down for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. This step is optional but adds a nice depth of flavor and better texture to the skin.
Build the base. Add the sliced onion and minced garlic to the bottom of your slow cooker. Pour in the chicken broth.
Add the chicken. Place the seasoned thighs on top of the onion and garlic layer, skin-side up if possible.
Cook low and slow. Cover and cook on LOW for 6 to 7 hours or on HIGH for 3 to 4 hours. The chicken is done when it reaches an internal temperature of 165°F and pulls apart easily with a fork.
Rest and portion. Remove the thighs and let them rest for 5 minutes. Pull the meat off the bone or leave whole, depending on how you plan to use it.
Store for the week. Divide into meal prep containers. Add rice, roasted vegetables, or whatever sides you like. Store in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze portions for up to 3 months.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 410 Protein 38g Carbs 4g Fat 27g Cost Per Serving $2.40 Nutrition is estimated for one bone-in chicken thigh with cooking juices. Values will vary slightly based on exact size of thighs.
Tips # Buy in bulk when thighs go on sale. Chicken thighs frequently drop to $0.99 to $1.49 per pound. Stock up and freeze them raw for a lower cost per serving. Don’t skip drying the chicken. Patting the thighs dry before seasoning helps the spices stick and gives you better browning if you sear. Use the cooking liquid. The juices left in the slow cooker are packed with flavor. Spoon them over your chicken when serving or use them as a base for a quick pan sauce. Remove the skin before storing if you want fewer calories. The skin adds fat but keeps the meat incredibly moist during cooking. Pull it off after cooking if you prefer a leaner option, dropping the fat content to around 14g per serving. Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are one of the best kept secrets in budget meal prep. This recipe gets you four solid meals with 40 grams of protein each, all for around $2.50 per serving. It pairs seasoned oven-baked thighs with rice and roasted broccoli, and the whole thing comes together in about an hour.
Why This Recipe Works # Chicken thighs cost significantly less per pound than chicken breasts, and they stay juicy even after reheating, which makes them ideal for meal prep. The simple spice rub builds real flavor without requiring anything fancy. Pairing them with rice and broccoli gives you a complete, balanced meal that reheats well every single day of the week.
Ingredients # For the chicken:
4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 2.5 lbs total) 1 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp onion powder 1/2 tsp salt 1/4 tsp black pepper For the sides:
2 cups dry white rice 4 cups broccoli florets (fresh or frozen) 1 tbsp olive oil (for broccoli) Salt and pepper to taste Estimated cost per serving: $2.40
Instructions # Preheat your oven to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with foil or parchment paper. If you are also roasting broccoli, use a second baking sheet or plan to add the broccoli halfway through.
Season the chicken. Pat the thighs dry with paper towels. Rub each piece with olive oil, then coat evenly with garlic powder, smoked paprika, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Place them skin-side up on the baking sheet.
Start cooking the rice. Add 2 cups of dry rice and 4 cups of water to a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 18 minutes. Remove from heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes before fluffing.
Roast the chicken. Place the baking sheet in the oven and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, until the skin is crispy and the internal temperature reaches 165°F. If you have a meat thermometer, use it. The thigh meat near the bone is what you are checking.

Ingredients # 2 cups (240g) rolled oats 6.3 oz (180g) vanilla protein powder 0.3 oz (9.2g) unflavored gelatin powder 3 tbsp (25g) cacao powder 1 tsp powdered stevia (adjust to taste) 1/2 tsp salt 5 cups (1140g) Greek yogurt or protein yogurt 3/4 cup water (adjust as needed for paste consistency) 6 thin Oreo cookies (one per serving) Cost per serving: ~$2.50 | Makes 6 servings
Instructions # Blend the dry ingredients. Add the oats, protein powder, gelatin, cacao powder, stevia, and salt to a blender. Blend until you have a fine, uniform powder. This step helps everything mix smoothly and gives you a better texture in the final product.
Make a paste. Pour the dry blend into a large mixing bowl. Slowly add the water a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you get a thick, smooth paste. You want it fully combined with no dry pockets. Start with half the water and add more as needed.
Add the yogurt. Spoon in the Greek or protein yogurt and stir until the paste and yogurt are completely combined. The mixture should be thick and uniform with a deep chocolate color.
Taste and adjust. Give it a quick taste and add a little more stevia if you want it sweeter. This is your chance to dial it in before it sets.
Divide into containers. Distribute the mixture evenly across 6 airtight containers or mason jars. Each portion should be roughly the same size.
Add the topping. Crumble one thin Oreo over the top of each container. You can swap for another cookie or even some crushed graham crackers if that is what you have on hand.
Refrigerate. Seal the containers and refrigerate for at least 6 hours. Overnight is ideal. The gelatin needs time to set and firm everything up into that cheesecake-style texture.

If you want a filling, high-protein meal that doesn’t wreck your grocery budget, this burrito bowl is it. We’re talking 42 grams of protein per serving for about $2.40, and it comes together in under 30 minutes. It’s also one of the best meals you can batch cook for the week.
Why This Recipe Works # Chicken thighs are cheaper than breasts and stay juicy even after reheating, which makes them ideal for meal prep. Canned black beans add a solid protein and fiber boost for almost nothing. Rice stretches everything out so you stay full for hours without spending more.
Ingredients # Serves 4
1.5 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs 1 cup long-grain white rice (dry) 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed 1 cup frozen corn 1 tbsp olive oil 2 tsp chili powder 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp garlic powder Salt and pepper to taste Optional toppings: salsa, plain Greek yogurt (instead of sour cream), shredded cheese Estimated cost per serving: ~$2.40
Instructions # Cook the rice. Combine 1 cup rice with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 18 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
Season the chicken. Pat your chicken thighs dry with a paper towel. Drizzle with olive oil, then coat with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Cook the chicken. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until the internal temperature hits 165°F. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice or chop it up.
Warm the beans and corn. In a small saucepan or microwave-safe bowl, heat the drained black beans and frozen corn together until warmed through, about 3 to 4 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and cumin if you like.
Assemble your bowls. Start with a base of rice, then layer on chicken, beans, and corn. Add your toppings of choice.
For meal prep: Store each component separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 4 days. Assemble when ready to eat.
Nutrition (Per Serving) # Nutrient Amount Calories 520 Protein 42g Carbs 52g Fat 12g Cost Per Serving ~$2.40 Nutrition estimates are based on the base recipe without optional toppings.
Tips # Swap the rice for cauliflower rice if you want to cut carbs. It keeps the cost similar and adds extra volume to your bowl. Buy chicken thighs in bulk when they go on sale and freeze them in 1.5 lb portions. This is one of the easiest ways to get your cost per serving even lower. Greek yogurt instead of sour cream adds extra protein and costs less per ounce at most stores. It tastes nearly identical in this bowl. Double the batch on Sunday and you’ve got lunch covered for the whole week. Each bowl reheats in about 2 minutes and holds up well without getting soggy. content:
If you only make one high-protein budget recipe this week, make this one. Four servings, 20 minutes, 34 grams of protein per bowl, and it costs about $2.30 a serving. The hot honey glaze turns basic ground beef into something that genuinely tastes like it came from a restaurant.
Jump to Recipe
Why This Recipe Works # Ground beef is one of the cheapest proteins per gram you can buy. The hot honey glaze — just honey, red pepper flakes, and a splash of vinegar — caramelises against the hot pan and creates little crispy edges on the beef that add real texture. Avocado and rice round it out into a complete, satisfying meal that keeps you full for hours.
Ingredients # For the bowl (4 servings):
1 lb (450g) 80/20 ground beef 2 cups cooked white rice (about 2/3 cup dry) 1 avocado, sliced 2 tablespoons soy sauce 1 tablespoon garlic, minced (about 3 cloves) 1 teaspoon sesame oil 2 green onions, sliced Salt and pepper to taste For the hot honey glaze:
3 tablespoons honey 1 to 2 teaspoons red pepper flakes 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar Cost per serving: ~$2.30
Instructions # Make the glaze. Whisk honey, red pepper flakes, and vinegar in a small bowl. Set aside. Cook the rice. Prepare according to package instructions. Day-old rice from the fridge works best. Brown the beef. Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add ground beef and break apart. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until browned through. Drain excess fat if needed. Add aromatics. Push beef to one side, add garlic to the cleared space and cook 30 seconds. Mix into the beef. Season. Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Stir and cook another minute until the beef looks glossy. Assemble. Divide rice between 4 bowls. Top with beef and sliced avocado. Finish. Drizzle hot honey glaze over each bowl. Garnish with green onions. Serve immediately. Nutrition (Per Serving) # Amount Calories ~480 kcal Protein 34g Carbohydrates 38g Fat 19g Cost per serving ~$2.30 Tips # Use 80/20 beef for the best flavour. The fat content keeps it juicy. Leaner beef works but add a teaspoon of olive oil to the pan. Adjust the heat. Start with 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes if you are sensitive to spice. You can always drizzle more at the table. Meal prep friendly. Store beef and rice separately in the fridge for up to 4 days. Slice fresh avocado each day. Push protein higher. Add a scoop of cottage cheese alongside the avocado for an extra 14g of protein per bowl. Related Recipes # Cheapest High Protein Foods: The Ultimate List Ground Turkey Meal Prep Bowls High Protein Egg Fried Rice The hot honey ground beef bowl is proof that eating high protein on a budget does not mean eating boring food. Make it once and it will earn a permanent spot in your weekly rotation.
